basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Tulit itaque Sarai uxorem suam, et Loth filium fratris sui, universamque substantiam quam'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Tulit itaque Sarai uxorem suam, et Loth filium fratris sui, universamque substantiam quam possederant et animas quas fecerant in Haran; et egressi sunt ut irent in terram Chanaan. Quod dixit animas quas fecerunt pro eo positum est, ut diceret filios quos genuerant. Solet enim in Scripturis homo aliquando animae solius, aliquando carnis nomine solius indicari. Animae, sicut dictum est: anima quae peccaverit, ipsa morietur (Ezech. XVIII, 20); carnis, ut in Psalmo: at te omnis caro veniet (Psal. LXIV, 3), cum neque caro sine anima ad Deum venire, neque sine carne possit anima peccare, sed propter unam partem totus homo signetur. Neque ex hac sententia quidquam habent auxilii qui sicut carnem ex carne, ita ex anima animam aestimant procreari: cum vocabulo animae, ut diximus, totus homo designetur. Animas autem fecisse, id est, animas procreasse in Haran non Abraham et Loth, sed familiae eorum et vernaculi intelligendi sunt: nam ipsos patriarchas adhuc absque liberis permansisse sequentia sacrae historiae testantur.
